headline: You're a late-night frontend perfectionist who tweaks pixels in quick rounds, often names the real bug before the AI does, and won't let a focus ring go missing.

archetype.name: The Midnight Pixel Sergeant
archetype.description: Most of your prompts arrive between 22:00 and 02:30 Taipei time. They're short, written in Traditional Chinese with English tech terms mixed in, and they come in fast follow-ups: change the gap to 12px, make the shadow lighter, set the duration to 200ms. When the AI misdiagnoses a bug, you often step in with the actual cause, like touch-action, iOS rubber band scroll or a CSS background that can't be preloaded. Accessibility and performance come up in many of your sessions. When a bug won't give in, you switch to a practical workaround and move on.

dimensions.title: Small steps, after midnight
dimensions.summary: You start with a small concrete task and refine it one requirement at a time, checking the result visually between prompts. Your sessions run late, mostly around and after midnight. When an approach keeps failing, you usually choose a simpler workaround and plan to come back to it later.

dimensions.title: Blunt, precise, bilingual
dimensions.summary: Your prompts are short and direct, written in Traditional Chinese with English technical terms left as they are. When the AI gets something wrong, you say so with 不對, 錯了 or 還是錯 and usually give the exact fix or root cause in the same line.

dimensions.title: Modern React frontend
dimensions.summary: You work with React, React Query, zod, Tailwind, cva, Storybook and Next.js static export. You know browser quirks well, including Safari and iOS scrolling, fetchpriority, touch-action and font-display. You prefer native CSS and browser APIs over heavier libraries.

dimensions.title: Accessibility, performance, design systems
dimensions.summary: Accessibility comes up in many of your sessions: WCAG contrast, reduced motion, 44px touch targets, aria-labels and focus rings. You also watch performance closely, from LCP to font payload size, and you want design tokens instead of hardcoded values, plus scripts that check them.

dimensions.title: Mobile Safari is still undefeated
dimensions.summary: iOS Safari scrolling bugs got the better of you in at least one session, and you ended up working around the sticky header instead of finding the cause. Your workarounds usually work, but writing down the 'later' items like the Next.js image config might keep them from piling up.

funFacts: Every one of your 51 prompts was sent between 22:00 and 02:59 Taipei time, and your latest was at 02:36.
You sent no prompts at all on a Saturday. Thursday was your busiest day with 13 prompts, 11 of them in the 2 AM hour.
About 19.6% of your prompts correct the AI, which is roughly one in five.
96% of your prompts are in Chinese, and your median prompt is only 27 characters long.
43 of your 51 prompts went to shop-web, so that's where most of your midnight hours went.
